name: NVR Essentials
headline: One course. Your whole team using NVR.
intro: Non-violent resistance training that helps your whole team respond as one when a young person's behaviour escalates.
glance: 6 hours in person, or 2 hours live online

problem.scene: 11pm. A young person is kicking the office door.
problem.question: What does your team do next?
with: The same response on every shift
Resist the behaviour, never the child
problem.standards: The Children's Homes Regulations and the Fostering National Minimum Standards expect de-escalation. Neither says what to say at 11pm. This course does.
problem.evidence: Honest about the evidence: early trials with parents are encouraging, research in care settings is still limited, and we say so on the day.

groups: Support workers, team leaders, registered managers
Carers, supervising social workers, team leaders
Deciding whether NVR fits your service

outcomes: Describe an escalation from the young person's side and the adult's, and how shouting or backing off feeds it.
Sort behaviours into those to resist, those to negotiate and those to let go.
Explain non-violent resistance (Haim Omer, 2004), the seven pillars and the three dimensions of adult presence.
Show how NVR supports the Children's Homes Regulations and Standard 3 of the Fostering National Minimum Standards.
Use cold-iron lines, delayed responses and baskets in a hot moment.
Plan a reconciliation gesture, an act of resistance and a first NVR session for your team.
story_line: One story runs through the day: Reece, 15, in a children's home. Reece is a composite, drawn from real experiences of care.

facilitator.name: Luke Rodgers BEM
facilitator.line: From care leaver to care leader
paras: Luke went into care at 10. He has spent his career inside children's services as a consultant, trainer and keynote speaker, and is CEO of The Care Leaders.
He has spent years helping children's homes put NVR into practice. With Durham County Council he brought NVR into 11 children's homes and trained 120 residential staff, online and face to face.
He led the national engagement on England's new fostering standards for the Department for Education, so he knows what the standards expect of the adults around a child, and where NVR fits.
He was a Knowledge Equity Fellow at Saïd Business School, University of Oxford, and was awarded the British Empire Medal in 2018 for commitment to children and families.

pillars.title: The 7 pillars of NVR
pillars.stance_line: Connection before correction. Calm, persistent adult presence sits over all seven pillars.
items: Stay calm and safe in the hot moment, and deal with it later.
Choose the one or two behaviours that matter most now, and let the rest go for a while.
Small acts of care, offered whatever happens, that say the relationship matters.
Calm, planned action that stops adults being controlled by aggression.
No one does this alone. Adults act together and in the open.
A written commitment: we will not use violence, and we will resist it.
Calm, persistent presence after an incident, made safe for residential care.
pillars.base: Non-violent resistance was developed by Haim Omer. The course covers every pillar, and the NVR Toolkit has a section on each.
